name: Capacity as a commitment
idea: Building capacity is hard to undo, so an announcement tells rivals how a firm means to compete.
suggests: Read an expansion as a signal about future prices and output, and ask what the firm gives up if it turns out wrong.
limits: Announcements are cheap and plants are slow to build, so the signal can be weaker than it looks.
competing_idea: Firms may expand only to follow demand, with no wish to signal anything to rivals.
questions: How costly would it be for the company to reverse this expansion?
How would rivals read this move?
What would the company do if demand fell short?

originals.reference: Illustrative reference, not a real work
